sources.entry: Sunshine - Remote game stream host for Moonlight with support up to 120 frames per second and 4K resolution. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C++/deb/Docker
Sunshine - Self-hosted game stream host for Moonlight. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Sunshine is a self-hosted game stream host that lets Moonlight clients connect and play games running on the host machine.
summary.what_it_does: Runs as a game streaming server for Moonlight clients on a variety of devices, offering low-latency streaming. It supports hardware encoding on AMD, Intel, and Nvidia GPUs, with software encoding also available. A web UI handles configuration and client pairing from a browser, either on the local server or from a mobile device. The README's compatibility tables cover gamepad emulation (generic, DualShock/DS4, DualSense/DS5, Switch Pro, Xbox 360/One/Series) and encoding APIs (AMF, Media Foundation, NVENC, QuickSync, VAAPI, Video Toolbox, Vulkan Video, software) across FreeBSD, Linux, macOS, and Windows. Screen capture methods vary by platform, including DXGI, KMS/DRM, NvFBC, ScreenCaptureKit, Wayland, X11, and XDG Desktop Portal. Full documentation is hosted on Read the Docs.
use_cases: stream games to another device on the home network
game streaming to phones, tablets, or TVs
configure game stream host via web browser
how_to_run: See the LizardByte documentation on Read the Docs for installation instructions
notable: Hardware encoding via AMD, Intel, and Nvidia GPUs, with software fallback
Web UI for configuration and client pairing
Broad platform matrix covering FreeBSD, Linux, macOS, and Windows
Multiple capture backends including Wayland, KMS/DRM, and XDG Desktop Portal
Virtual gamepad emulation for several controller types
caveats: Gamepad emulation on macOS and Windows for some profiles needs a separately installed, licensed Virtual HID Broker, and some features are missing on FreeBSD and Linux
Many encoder and capture combinations are unsupported or partial depending on OS and GPU
README states system requirement tables are a work in progress and should not be used for hardware purchases
